verses.text: So now there is no condemnation for those who belong to Christ Jesus. They do not live by their sinful human nature, but by the Spirit.
For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit, who gives life, has set me free from the law of sin and death.

The law of Moses could not save us, because our sinful human nature made it weak. But God did what the law could not do. He sent his own Son in a body like our sinful bodies, to be an offering for sin. In this way God passed judgement on sin in a human body.
He did this so that the right standard of the law would be fully met in us, who do not live by our sinful nature but by the Spirit.
People who live by their sinful nature set their minds on what that nature wants. But people who live by the Spirit set their minds on what the Spirit wants.
A mind controlled by the sinful nature leads to death. But a mind controlled by the Spirit leads to life and peace.
The sinful mind is an enemy of God. It does not obey God's law, and it cannot.
So those who are controlled by their sinful nature cannot please God.
But you are not controlled by your sinful nature. You are controlled by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you. Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him.
But if Christ lives in you, your body will die because of sin, yet the Spirit gives you life because God has made you right with him.

The Spirit of God raised Jesus from the dead. If that same Spirit lives in you, then God, who raised Christ from the dead, will also give life to your bodies that die. He will do this through his Spirit, who lives in you.
So, my brothers and sisters, we have a duty, but it is not to our sinful nature. We do not have to live the way it wants.
If you live by your sinful nature, you will die. But if, through the Spirit, you put to death the sinful things you do, you will live.
All who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God.
The Spirit you received does not make you slaves who live in fear again. Instead, you received the Spirit who makes you God's own children. By him we cry out, "Abba, Father."
The Spirit himself joins with our spirit to assure us that we are God's children.
And if we are his children, then we will receive what God has promised to his children. We will share it with Christ. But if we share in his suffering, we will also share in his glory.
I am sure that what we suffer now is nothing compared with the glory that will be shown to us later.
All of creation is waiting with eager hope for the day when God will show who his children really are.
Creation was made subject to emptiness and decay. This was not its own choice. It was the will of God, who made it so, but there was hope.
The hope is that creation itself will be set free from its slavery to decay. It will share in the glorious freedom of God's children.
We know that the whole of creation has been groaning together, like a woman in the pains of giving birth, right up to now.

And not only creation. We too groan inside ourselves, even though we have the Spirit as the first part of God's gift. We are waiting eagerly for God to make us fully his children, which includes setting our bodies free.
We were saved with this hope in our hearts. But hope that can already be seen is not really hope. Who hopes for something they already have?
But if we hope for something we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently.
In the same way, the Spirit helps us when we are weak. We do not know what we ought to pray for. But the Spirit himself prays for us with groans that words cannot express.
God, who searches our hearts, knows what the Spirit is thinking, because the Spirit prays for God's people in the way God wants.
And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love him, those he has called according to his plan.
God knew his people before they were born, and he chose them to become like his Son. In this way his Son would be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters.
Those he chose, he also called. Those he called, he also made right with himself. And those he made right with himself, he also gave a share in his glory.
So what can we say about all this? If God is on our side, who can be against us?
God did not hold back even his own Son, but gave him up for all of us. Since he did that, will he not also freely give us everything else, together with Christ?
Who can bring any charge against the people God has chosen? It is God himself who declares them not guilty.
Who then can condemn them? Christ Jesus died for us. More than that, he was raised to life. He is at the right hand of God, and he is praying for us.
Who can separate us from the love of Christ? Can trouble, hardship, persecution, hunger, poverty, danger or violent death?
As the Scriptures say, "Because of you we face death all day long. We are treated like sheep that are led to be killed."
No! In all these things we win an overwhelming victory through Christ, who loved us.
I am fully convinced that nothing can separate us from God's love. Not death or life, not angels or ruling spirits, not anything now or anything in the future, not any powers,
not anything high above or deep below, nor anything else in all creation. Nothing can separate us from the love of God that is ours in Christ Jesus our Lord.
